unitSkip: Optional standalone billing fixture is included in the shared real PostgreSQL suite.
tested: Real source and HTTPS authority databases preserve distinct worker allowances across server restart.
The worker leaves a target intact and avoids provider deletion when the required allowance cannot fit. Outcome reservations are all or nothing.
An unchanged failed provider retry creates no new outbox event. A lost completion observation recovers from the durable allowance and original source commit without calling the provider again.
A new request refused at capacity rolls back its source acceptance and leaves no checkpoint claim. The existing worker spends its reserved final slot and completes.
The application role cannot call the worker probe, and a wrong worker lease returns no facts.
limits: The near-capacity fixture seeds the checkpoint counters. The separate restart, archive and replay tests verify complete real histories.

The worker protects each irreversible step; a pending job can still wait at capacity. Hosted activation, operational alerts, a capacity lifecycle policy and real provider verification are separate requirements.
Default operations remain cleanup-only. Legacy local fixtures use their existing trusted writer. Hosted source and authority were not modified.
